title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: protect files in excluded Windows folders
summary: The rollout dates, prerequisite client version and existing exclusion controls are supported. However, the briefing treats licensing as unpublished despite Microsoft's published licensing rule for Windows endpoint protections, and labels the new control tenant-wide without evidence of its configuration scope.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing exclusions leave files created or modified in those locations outside Endpoint DLP policy enforcement.
claims.quote: Any files that you create or modify in those locations aren't subject to DLP policy enforcement.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Learn lists two AppData paths as excluded by default on Windows.
claims.quote:
Windows file paths excluded by default
- `%SystemDrive%\\Users\\*(1)\\AppData\\Roaming`
- `%SystemDrive%\\Users\\*(1)\\AppData\\Local`

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Applications write files to app-data and temporary folders.
claims.quote: Within its app data store, each app has system-defined root directories: one for local files, one for roaming files, and one for temporary files. Your app can add new files and new containers to each of these root directories.

claims.quote: Searched: read MC1384420 in full, including Platforms, Action Required / Recommendations and Compliance considerations; it describes no identity or permission change.

claims.where: controls[0]; What's changing; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout

claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP protected excluded folders Windows AppData protection licensing roles enable Set-PolicyConfig'; 'Endpoint DLP protected exclusion paths Set-PolicyConfig'. Opened Configure endpoint DLP settings and Set-PolicyConfig; neither documents this new protection switch.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because Microsoft has not published whether existing Endpoint DLP licences cover this extension.
claims.quote: This licensing model enables you to apply Microsoft Purview controls and protections to Microsoft 365 and Windows/macOS endpoint-based assets. It's described in the Microsoft Purview service description.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace the licensing notes and 'Whether this change follows the same licensing is not yet published' with: 'Existing Endpoint DLP licensing applies to Windows endpoint protections; the eligible suites are listed in the Microsoft Purview service description. No change-specific additional licence has been published as of November 2026.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-billing-models alongside the existing service-description source. Keep uncertainty limited to any additional change-specific requirement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The service description includes Endpoint DLP in the suites named in the briefing.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW and Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection & Governance
Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) | Included

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No additional licence specific to this change is published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP excluded folders license'; read the roadmap record, MC1384420, Purview service description and Purview billing models. Found existing Endpoint DLP licensing, but no additional licence specific to excluded-folder protection.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No meter is documented specifically for this change.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP excluded folders meter'; opened the Purview service description and Purview billing models. The billing page places Windows/macOS endpoint assets under per-user licensing and documents no meter for excluded-folder protection.

claims.where: Scope
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published the administrator roles for configuring the new setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP excluded folders role'; 'Endpoint DLP excluded folders licensing roles PowerShell'. Read MC1384420, Configure endpoint DLP settings and Set-PolicyConfig; no role is named for the new protection setting.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls; Scope
claims.claim: Existing Windows exclusions are configured at Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > File path exclusions for Windows.
claims.quote: go to Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > File path exclusions for Windows.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig -EndpointDlpGlobalSettings @(@{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="<path>"}) configures an existing path exclusion.
claims.quote:
The EndpointDlpGlobalSettings parameter specifies the global endpoints.
Example values:
- `@{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="C:\Windows";}`
- `@{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="%AppData%\Mozilla";}`

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope
claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[1].scope
claims.claim: The existing Windows folder exclusion setting has tenant scope.
claims.quote: Centrally configured settings control many aspects of endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) behavior. These settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: The new excluded-folder protection control has tenant-wide configuration scope.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP protected exclusion paths tenant'. Read MC1384420, Configure endpoint DLP settings and Set-PolicyConfig. The notice requires policy updates but does not state the new control's scope; Learn documents only the existing exclusions.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].scope to 'other' and add 'Configuration scope not yet published' to its note; mirror these changes in the rendered first row. Keep the existing open question about per-path, per-policy or tenant-wide configuration.

claims.where: Governance controls; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP protected excluded folders Windows AppData protection licensing roles enable Set-PolicyConfig'; 'Endpoint DLP protected exclusion paths tenant'. Read MC1384420 and the settings and cmdlet references; none explains the interaction.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The change extends existing Endpoint DLP policies and their audit or block actions to protected excluded folders.

claims.where: rationale: impact
claims.claim: The users affected by enforcement are those covered by the Endpoint DLP policy scope, rather than automatically every user.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP policies can be scoped to users logging into onboarded devices. Policies are evaluated when a scoped user logs onto an onboarded device.
